claims.claim: ASRT visual instructions present four locations, participant selects one of four corresponding key responses each trial; 8-element alternating deterministic/random design produces controlled context-specific trigram probabilities.

Participants practice over ten sessions, first eight original sequence, session9 interference new alternating sequence, session10 switches old/new epochs; session1-8 and changed condition not a spontaneously selected model goal.
Trial t external required visual event e_t and participant actual key press k_t must be distinct on error trials; observed RT is experimental latency, not a predicted action command.

Model obtains the externally generated complete e_1:t sequence, observed k_t and response latency for participant fitting, rather than predicting future real-world action outcomes with closed motor loop.
Nonparametric DP distribution over categorical labels, prior strength alpha and base H, uses probability-reinforcing reuse for observed categories.
ddCRP extends DP with exponential trial-distance-dependent customer-link weights, lambda level-specific; recency of samples affects memory and prediction.
claims.source: main p8 Eq2 Fig3b; S1 p2

claims.claim: ddHDP for context u_t=(e_t-n,...,e_t-1), with strength alpha_|u|, decay lambda_|u| and suffix parent predictive distribution G_pi(u).
claims.source: main p8 Eq3 Fig3c; S1 p2

claims.claim: Prediction recursion at exhausted context n=0 returns 1/L uniform categorical label distribution, not a learned world-model transition system.
Maximum depth N and hierarchy of N+1 levels are imposed by analyst/model specification; individual restaurants for observed contexts arise from sequence history.
Customer-seating c indexed by context u, candidate label l and timestamps; local old-label strength sums exp(-delta/lambda_|u|) across past same-context events.

CUSTOMER_PROB starts from longest available suffix context, combines recency-weighted old label mass with alpha_n times recursively backed-off suffix probability; normalized by all customers plus alpha_n.

After observing actual event e_t, ADD_CUSTOMER inserts a new timestamp-labelled customer in the corresponding restaurant and stochastically terminates or propagates to suffix lower level according to weighted old vs alpha_n times suffix label probability.
At each trial, prediction scores the actually pressed key k_t first, but updates customer seating using instructed event e_t, not the possibly mistaken key k_t.

Published parser uses five stochastic seating samples to estimate prediction probabilities; their numerical stability tests are limited to the sampled original data, not an exact analytic posterior proof.

Individual categorical press/event labels are not executed multistep motor options; n-gram predictive context and seating hierarchy provide task-conditioned 'chunks', not a demonstrated motor-controller macro-executor.

The model can adapt effective prediction context weighting as counts, recency and fitted hyperparameters change; finite levels and backoff architecture are designed in advance; no new unbounded type of cognitive coordinator learned.

Log response time is modeled by a prediction-probability term and low-level repetition/spatial-distance/error/posterror covariates in a joint participant-specific regression; observed RT is not model-produced action.

Random search over strength/decay parameters (1000 draws), repeated fits and MAP selection with session/epoch priors and OLS coefficients; withheld RT may occur mid-epoch while model still sees actual sequence events.
Short context is last up to N e-events; long-term evidence remains as decaying timestamped customer memories, not independently learned persistent declarative skill objects.
Source S2 compares direct trigram ddCRP, uniform interpolation of independent n-level ddCRPs, deterministic stacked Katz-like backoff and ddHCRP main; all forget via distance dependence.

ddUCRP reproduces observed smoothing but underestimates trigram effect; ddSCRP and trigram baseline lack smoothing; HCRP fits selected combined criteria better, not a proof only hierarchy can cause behavior.
claims.source: S2 p4 TableA FigD; p6 FigF

claims.claim: Model matches session-scale inferred context gain and forgetting dynamics, but fitted parameters, inferred representations and subject behavior remain inferential and model-dependent.
Uncorrected complex/spatial WM hyperparameter correlations reported p=.01/.02 but neither survives BH over 24 comparisons (adjusted .09/.28); verbal WM none.
Human old/new skill maintenance jointly stable with positive cross-ability during interference; single forgetful HCRP trades old for new and incorrectly predicts zig-zag when epochs alternate.
Paper suggests TWO independent HCRPs plus an arbiter might rescue parallel old/new stability, but does not implement or fit such arbiter in original model.
Source first-session group >2 effect nonsignificant for measured RT p=.084 and HCRP p=.199; session8 mean p=.080/.076, despite some individual variability fits.
Stationary trigram and HCRP explain similar overall response-time variance; additional selected behavioral probes are required to distinguish hidden context hierarchy.

Error RT patterns include response/pattern/recency errors and original observation-bound motor covariates, not direct proof underlying individual cognitive representation matches fitted seating states.
Original published fits, individual fitted alpha/lambda, p-values and figure trajectories are author reports; no W4 exact code/data or original numerical rerun is claimed.
Paper explicitly adapts hierarchical language sequence priors and ddCRP plus ASRT experimental literature; does not invent the DP or the motor task.
Publisher article visually displayed no correction banner and targeted title search found no separate public correction hit at this check; definitive correction-free history remains not proven.
Defining S1 S1.A-C and S2 four alternative equations+model comparison figures are part of P19 original published source; omitting them would misrepresent generative/update and unfavorable findings.
claims.source: main Supporting information; first-party S1/S2 raw
